prior_findings_note: P1-P13 and N1-N15 were NOT reopened. Sol's N14/N15 confirm P12 and P1-P11 stand. Edits are confined to the baseline/R17 surface that P13A and P14 name.

P13A.finding: The receipt had two shapes (a top-level commands array initially vs named captures[] entries for regeneration and citation), no rule that the initial capture is captures[0], and it required git_status_clean === true in a planning worktree that is necessarily dirty with the reviewed Flow artifacts - so the required initial receipt could not truthfully be produced.
P13A.resolution: One versioned schema is now used from the first capture onward. Immutable top level, written once: schema, schema_version 1, spec_id, base_sha bb994b580356a41a31093fea85b06993c1a18e4c, canonical_commands, captures: []. The contradictory top-level commands array and top-level git_status_clean/environment/timestamp block are removed explicitly (the artifacts now state there is no such top level). captures[] is append-only and its FIRST entry is the initial capture; every entry - initial and regenerated alike - is a complete self-contained object carrying capture_id (unique, cited later), regenerated (false initially), reason (null initially, otherwise why), base_sha, worktree evidence (path, create command, verified head_sha, empty git status --porcelain), setup (the bun install --frozen-lockfile run inside that worktree, with confirmation the lockfile was unchanged), commands[] (per canonical command: exact string, exit status, duration, counts, enumerated failures[], raw-log path and sha256), environment (Bun and tsc versions, platform/arch/uname, env notes), started_at/finished_at, and planning_worktree_state. The INITIAL capture now executes in an isolated detached worktree at the exact base SHA (git worktree add --detach -> verify head_sha and empty status -> bun install --frozen-lockfile inside that worktree only -> canonical commands -> git worktree remove) - identical in shape to regeneration. Cleanliness is asserted in that isolated worktree, never in the planning worktree: the planning worktree's dirt is recorded separately as planning_worktree_state evidence, asserted to contain no product-path changes, and is never required clean and never gates the capture. The capture-before-product-change ordering, the append-only regeneration rule, and citation of the final comparison by capture_id are preserved.

P14.finding: Baseline and final command sets diverged: task .2 captured bun test test/serve/ but neither full bun test nor bun run docs:verify, while task .7 ran both and treated any failure absent from the baseline list as new - so a pre-existing failure outside test/serve/ or in docs verification would be misclassified as new.
P14.resolution: One explicit canonical baseline-compared command list (CBC), identical in strings, order, and parsing, shared verbatim by spec R17, task .2's receipt (canonical_commands) and task .7's final gate: (1) bun run lint:check, (2) bunx tsc --noEmit, (3) bun test (full suite, replacing the former test/serve/ subset), (4) bun run test:web, (5) bun run docs:verify. Task .7's final gate now runs those five verbatim and diffs EACH command's failures against THAT SAME command's enumerated failures[] in the cited capture - no subset, superset, or reformulation. Everything outside the CBC is defined consistently as an absolute-pass gate that is never baseline-compared: the new tests this spec adds, bun run test:e2e:pdf, bun run test:package, and the P-1...P-6 budgets. Tasks .1 and .3-.6 keep focused subsets for fast feedback, with a stated rule that a focused failure is checked against the enumerated failures of the CBC command containing it (bun test for test files, bun run test:web for the web DOM suite) and that task .7's verbatim CBC run is the authoritative comparison. The spec's compatibility bullet was aligned to the same list.

consistency_audit.canonical_command_list: The identical five-command list appears in spec R17, task .2 step 0 + acceptance, and task .7 final gate + acceptance. No artifact still names `bun test test/serve/` as a baseline-captured command.
consistency_audit.receipt_schema: Only one schema is described anywhere. The surviving mentions of a top-level commands array and git_status_clean are the explicit negations stating they do not exist.
consistency_audit.clean_tree_semantics: No artifact requires the planning worktree to be clean. Cleanliness is asserted only inside the isolated detached worktree; the spec's execution-order paragraph was aligned to the same wording.
consistency_audit.capture_id_citation: Spec R17, task .2, and task .7 all use capture_id citation; append-only regeneration preserved in all three.

subsequent_corrections.label: addendum
subsequent_corrections.what_was_wrong: This transaction required EVERY captures[] entry, including regenerated ones, to assert that planning_worktree_state contains no product-path changes. That assertion is true only for the initial capture: task .7 permits regeneration after tasks .1-.6 have implemented the feature, when the planning worktree necessarily holds product, test, dependency, lockfile, and documentation changes. As written, a regenerated capture could not be recorded truthfully.
subsequent_corrections.note: Everything else recorded in this receipt stands as executed and verified at the time; only the per-capture planning_worktree_state assertion scope was subsequently narrowed to the initial capture.
